scenes.heading: Editing Templates — Initial Content & Layout
scenes.narration: Templates. Editing Templates — Initial Content & Layout. In this video we review 8 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is Initial Content mode used for?
scenes.heading: A mode used to define content that will appear when a page is first created based on the template
scenes.body: Initial Content mode is used to define content that will appear when a page is first created based on the template. It can be thought of as edit mode for pages created with that template, and can then be edited by page authors.
scenes.narration: What is Initial Content mode used for? A mode used to define content that will appear when a page is first created based on the template. scenes.question: In Initial Content mode, which components can be selected and edited even though all Structure-mode content is visible?
scenes.heading: Only components that have been unlocked can be selected and edited
scenes.body: Although all content created in Structure mode is visible in Initial Content mode, only components that have been unlocked can be selected and edited there.
scenes.narration: In Initial Content mode, which components can be selected and edited even though all Structure-mode content is visible? Only components that have been unlocked can be selected and edited. Although all content created in Structure mode is visible in Initial Content mode, only components that have been unlocked can be selected and edited there.

scenes.question: In which mode are policies defined for a template, Structure or Initial Content?
scenes.heading: In Structure mode — policies are not defined in Initial Content mode
scenes.body: Policies are not defined in Initial Content mode but rather in Structure mode. Initial Content mode is used purely to set up the starting content page authors will see.

scenes.question: What visual indicator shows an unlocked, editable component when selected in Initial Content mode?
scenes.heading: A blue border
scenes.body: Unlocked components that are available for editing are marked, and when selected they display a blue border, distinguishing them from locked structural components.
scenes.narration: What visual indicator shows an unlocked, editable component when selected in Initial Content mode? A blue border. Unlocked components that are available for editing are marked, and when selected they display a blue border, distinguishing them from locked structural components.

scenes.question: What becomes possible in Initial Content mode if a container component was unlocked in Structure mode?
scenes.heading: You can add new components to it, using the Drag components here area or the Insert New Component toolbar option
scenes.body: If a container component has been unlocked in Structure mode, you can add new components to the container in Initial Content mode, using either the Drag components here area or the Insert New Component option from the container's toolbar.

scenes.question: What can page authors do with components added inside an unlocked container in Initial Content mode?
scenes.heading: They can be moved or deleted on resulting pages
scenes.body: Components added in Initial Content mode (inside an unlocked container) can be moved on or deleted from resulting pages, unlike components fixed in Structure mode.

scenes.question: If you update a template's initial content after pages already exist, are those existing pages affected?
scenes.heading: No — only pages created after the change will reflect the updated initial content
scenes.body: If the initial content of the template is updated after pages are created based on the template, those existing pages will not be affected by changes to the initial content — only pages created afterward pick it up.

scenes.question: What does Layout mode let a template author configure?
scenes.heading: Defining the template's layout for different device formats, similar to how layout works in page authoring
scenes.body: In Layout mode, a template author can design the layout of a template for different devices, ensuring a responsive design that adapts to various screen sizes, similar to how page authoring works for responsiveness.
